title: California's 21st Congressional District General Election, 2026
description: The general election for California's 21st Congressional District will be held on November 3, 2026, following a top-two primary on June 2, 2026. Incumbent Democratic Rep. Jim Costa, first elected in 2004, advances to face Republican businessman Kyle Kirkland. The district covers parts of Fresno and Tulare counties in the Central Valley and has a Democratic voter registration advantage (40.8% D, 27.5% R), with a Cook Partisan Voting Index of D+5 following redistricting under Proposition 50. Costa, a moderate Democrat and member of the Blue Dog Coalition, emphasizes his record on water infrastructure and agriculture, while Kirkland runs as a political outsider focused on the cost of living and government accountability.
polling_note: No publicly available opinion polls were found for this race as of the research date.

candidates.name: Jim Costa
candidates.summary: Jim Costa is the Democratic incumbent representing California's 21st Congressional District, first elected in 2004. A third-generation Central Valley farmer and former California State Assemblymember and State Senator, he serves on the House Agriculture and Foreign Affairs Committees and is a member of the moderate Blue Dog Coalition. Costa prioritizes water infrastructure, agricultural policy, and the California High-Speed Rail project.

candidates.name: Kyle Kirkland
candidates.summary: Kyle Kirkland is a Republican businessman and political outsider running for Congress in CA-21. He is the owner of Club One Casino in Fresno, President of the California Gaming Association, and former Chairman of Steinway Musical Instruments. Kirkland emphasizes his business background, calling for reduced regulation, lower costs of living, government accountability, and border security.

forecast.rationale: No public polling is available for this race, so the forecast relies on district fundamentals. CA-21 has a Democratic voter registration edge (40.8% to 27.5% R) and a Cook PVI of D+5, indicating a Democratic-leaning Central Valley district. Incumbent Jim Costa (first elected 2004) brings long tenure, high name recognition, and a moderate Blue Dog profile suited to this agricultural district. Republican Kyle Kirkland is a credible businessman and political outsider with sufficient resources to compete, but lacks the partisan baseline advantage or name recognition of the incumbent. Without race-specific polling, confidence is medium, but the combination of incumbency, Democratic lean, and registration advantage makes Costa a clear favorite. Expected margin in the mid-to-high single digits.
